```python
iommu=Int('iommu')
np=Int('np')
hbase=Int('hbase')
dbase=Int('dbase')
dsize=Int('dsize')
fbase=Int('fbase')
fsize=Int('fsize')
hend=Int('hend')
htab_address=Int('htab_address')
htab_size_bytes=Int('htab_size_bytes')

# Assume pointer "iommu" is NULL
s.add(iommu == 0)

# Line 83: if(!(hbase == 0)) - branch taken when hbase is non-zero
# This branch is reached only when (fbase + fsize) > 0x800000000ul
# hbase = __pa(htab_address), so hbase is derived from htab_address
# htab_address must be non-NULL (checked earlier with if(!htab_address) return -1)
s.add(htab_address != 0)

# hbase is non-zero in this branch
s.add(hbase != 0)

# hbase = __pa(htab_address) - physical address, non-zero
# hend = hbase + htab_size_bytes
s.add(hend == hbase + htab_size_bytes)

# Segment alignment constraints (must hold to reach this point)
# hbase == ALIGN(hbase, 1 << IO_SEGMENT_SHIFT)
# hend == ALIGN(hend, 1 << IO_SEGMENT_SHIFT)
# These are alignment properties; represent as hbase being a multiple of segment size
# (skipping exact alignment since IO_SEGMENT_SHIFT value is uncertain)

# np is a valid axon node pointer inside the loop
s.add(np != 0)
```
